value.body: Map data analysts keep digital maps accurate. They work at mapping and navigation firms, geospatial service companies and outsourcing centres, editing roads, buildings, addresses and points of interest by checking them against satellite imagery, street-level photos and field reports. A typical day is a queue of map edits or quality checks against a set of guidelines.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BA or B.Sc in Geography, or any graduate with map-reading skills

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Map editing tools, QGIS or ArcGIS, satellite imagery viewers

items.label: Common starting titles
items.value: Map analyst, GIS data associate, geospatial annotator

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many entry roles are filled through walk-ins or aptitude tests at geospatial service firms, which train new hires on their own editing tools. A geography background helps with map reading and coordinate systems; a short GIS certificate (QGIS or ArcGIS) makes an application stronger.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Reading maps, satellite imagery and coordinate systems
Basic GIS software such as QGIS

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is often target-based and repetitive, with shift timings in some firms.
Common next steps: senior map analyst, quality reviewer, or a GIS analyst role.
Learning GIS analysis or Python scripting helps move beyond editing work.
